utterances.text: Yes, the next number would be 3/301.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: There is my copy. If the English version could be placed on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MILOS JANKOVIC
utterances.text: May I take it out?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like, actually, to use the copy that I handed you, if that's all right, Mr. Jankovic, because that's the copy that we received from your counsel. Can you take a look at the first page, please. Do you see your signature on that document?

utterances.speaker: MILOS JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you open up the document, please. Turn the page, please. You see in the first page, is that a copy of the document, the statement that you gave to counsel for Mr. Prcac?

utterances.speaker: MILOS JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it coincides with my own photocopy.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please turn to the next page and then the following page, and I'm wondering if we can pull back -- there we go. That's a good view.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Jankovic, could you take a look at the first page, please, of your witness statement. It begins, "In April 1992, I was working in the Prijedor Public Security Centre as head of the communications and communications security department." Do you see that? You can look at it right in front of you, sir, in your own language. It's right in front of you on the table.

utterances.speaker: MILOS JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And the next sentence says, "I was working in that capacity on 29 April 1992." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then a little bit lower down you talk about a meeting that took place in the Public Security Centre, and you say that, "The meeting was not scheduled in advanced." Do you see that? "We were summoned verbally that day and there was no agenda." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And lower down you begin to discuss the receipt of a dispatch. Do you see that in that large paragraph that fills up much of the page where you say, "I took the dispatch for the chief of the Prijedor CJB and I returned to the meeting." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I can't find it just now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Take your time, take your time, it's okay.

utterances.speaker: MILOS JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me where it is, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, right in the middle of the page: "The communications officer called me because the duty communications officer from the Banja Luka CSB had refused to connect him," and then there's a discussion of a dispatch which you took to the chief of the Prijedor station himself. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MILOS JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you see any mention of the date April 27th in the statement that you gave to counsel for Mr. Prcac?

utterances.speaker: MILOS JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MILOS JANKOVIC
utterances.text: It's not mentioned here. I don't see any mention of it. I see that it is not mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you mentioned --

utterances.speaker: MILOS JANKOVIC
utterances.text: It says the 29th, but that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You talk about a meeting that occurred on the 29th in your statement and receiving this dispatch on the 29th of April, 1992. What I want to know is, which version is correct, what you told the Trial Chamber today or what you put in this statement that you signed about a month ago?

utterances.speaker: MILOS JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I asked the attorney, because I was dictating this dispatch to an old typist who made several mistakes, and I asked him to tell you to allow me to correct these mistakes. In addition to this mistake, this is a mistake that I noticed myself subsequently, but I had already given a copy to the attorney. There's another mistake in line 28, first word. It says, SJB, SJB -- inside of Banja Luka it should be Bosanski Novi. It was an elderly man who was typing it. This was all done in haste. I noticed some errors as I went along, but as you see, these mistakes went unnoticed. It was not the 29th of April. That was two days later when a takeover of power took place. That is certainly not correct. What is correct is what I am saying. And also instead of this Bosanski Novi, there are other stylistic errors. For example, the way a dispatch is to be delivered, the typist didn't put it properly. He was typing more quickly than I was speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Jankovic, did you review the statement before you signed it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I did, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And did you understand that it was important that this statement be accurate when you signed it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did understand it was important, and I paid most attention to the contents and less to things like numbers. And you see, again, it says Banja Luka, which is incorrect. It should be Bosanski Novi. There might be another error that I still haven't managed to notice.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, let's move away from this statement, because we don't have a lot of time today, and talk about the document that you read out a short time ago. That was the order dated, by the way, 29th of April, 1992, signed by Alija Delimustafic, and I just have a couple of questions that I want to ask you about that order.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And perhaps a copy of that order could be placed back on the ELMO, if we have an English version, please. Can we place the English version on the ELMO and provide the witness with a copy of the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You see the date on that order, Mr. -- you see the -- do you see the date on that order, Mr. Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS JANKOVIC
utterances.text: That is the wrong -- this is the TO. I need the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, this is the one I want to talk about. This is the one you read out a few minutes ago. I want to talk about this document. Could you just put it down for a minute. Do you see the date on this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Jovan Simic. Mr. Jovan Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the order that he read was signed by Delimustafic, so that is the statement that the witness is talking about all the time. If necessary, he should be given the statement that he read, I would suggest to my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Absolutely. I apologise if I was incorrect. That's what I thought had just been placed on the ELMO. Apparently I was wrong. Thank you for clarifying that. Can we place on the ELMO a copy of what the witness read previously. Is this it? All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you see the date on that order, Mr. Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Saxon, is this a document marked 44, D44/5; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I believe, yes, Your Honour. I believe so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not asking, I am stating that this is a document that has been marked D44/5.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you see the date on the top of that document, Mr. Jankovic? It says 29 April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MILOS JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now, during the night of the 29th of April, 1992, and in the morning of the 30th, power in Prijedor was taken over by Serb authorities; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Let's just focus on this order or this dispatch just for a -- very briefly. On the 29th of April, or even if it was the 27th of April, 1992, as you mentioned, Bosnia and Herzegovina still existed as a recognised state, did it not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jovan Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my learned friend is testifying. Bosnia-Herzegovina in those days was not a recognised state. It was part of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. My learned friend is attempting to testify and mislead the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is a way of putting questions, making a statement and then asking whether the witness agrees or not. It is not my preferred method, but I think that the Prosecutor, and the Defence for that matter, has the right to do it, and the witness can say, "Yes, I agree" or "I disagree." As I have said, it is not my preference but I respect differences in our methods. Yes, Mr. Jovan Simic?

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Quite true, Your Honour, but such a method could be applied when talking to somebody who is familiar with these things and who was directly involved. But this is a person who does not fit into that category, especially with respect to dates. Two or three months for him may not mean much. So it would be better, I think, to rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us hear the reply of the witness. And then, if necessary, if you need additional questions, you can put them to the witness. What was your question, Mr. Saxon?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: My question was, on the 29th of April, or even if it was the 27th of April, 1992, if you know, was Bosnia and Herzegovina a recognised state? If you know.

utterances.speaker: MILOS JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I never focused on all the information outside the work I did, because my professional orientation was such that I never allowed politics to have any effect on me. So I don't remember any dates, when Bosnia-Herzegovina was recognised, when Yugoslavia ceased to exist, et cetera. I never even wanted to know those dates. All I knew how to do was to respect my superior and abide by the rules, on condition that I was not asked to do something that was outside the law and I knew what I could do and what I should not do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, then, why, then, did this order cause so much excitement?

utterances.speaker: MILOS JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I never knew that it would cause excitement. To this day, I don't know why. Some people said it was a good thing, some people said it wasn't. It was marked "very urgent" and that means as quickly as possible, and that is what I did. I took it in person because there were no signalman around and I was the chief. But as they were not there, I had no choice but to carry it myself. I give the signalman -- gave the signalman a book to take note of the dispatch, to sign that he had received it, and I carried out my duties according to the book --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you, to your knowledge, was a copy of this order published in the local Prijedor paper in July of 1992, Kozarski Vjesnik?

utterances.speaker: MILOS JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was. I can't tell you how many days later, a couple of days after the takeover of power, Simo Drljaca called me to go to his office and there I found several men whom I didn't know. Simo asked me whether this dispatch existed. He said that some journalists had reported on it, and he told me to bring it to him if I had it. I said that according to the rules of service, it does not exist but -- since the crypto material is destroyed and burnt every ten days. But since it was still not ten days, maybe we could find it. And the signalman found the tape, made another copy. I brought it to Simo. He gave it to this man. I don't know who the man was. And I left. A couple of days later, I saw a photocopy of it in the Vjesnik paper, newspaper, Kozarski Vjesnik newspaper.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You told us that shortly after this order was received, power was taken over in Prijedor by Serb authorities. Can you describe how the takeover of Prijedor was carried out? Who organised it? Who directed it? Which police units participated in the takeover?

utterances.speaker: MILOS JANKOVIC
utterances.text: That evening, it was in the evening, it was already getting dark, though it was early summer. I was in my apartment. Whenever there were urgent meetings, and if I was convened as the chief of department, my signalman knew where I was and he would call me. I was called and told to go to Cirkin Polje. There were a lot of people congregating there. Some people I knew, workers from our own Public Security Station, but there were far more people whom I did not know. This was in the evening, darkness was falling. And during the night, as a signalman, I didn't have anything to do there. I just had to show up. And that was the first time I saw Simo Drljaca. He came and introduced himself and said that by decision of, I think, the SDS, he said that from now on, he would be the chief of the Public Security Station and I accepted him as such. As I had nothing to do, I was just present there, I sat there in this room. There were several rooms in this building, and they were getting together. I think there were small groups. I saw that some of them had weapons. Whether they distributed those weapons there or not, I can't say because I didn't see it. Anyway, those who took over power left. None of us slept that night. And when they took control of the Public Security Station and other facilities --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think we've heard a lot regarding the conflict, because, as you know, there is a decision on judicial notice regarding the conflict. Do you need all this information, Mr. Saxon?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, and I realise we are out of time. I will pose one more question and I will sit down, if that's all right with the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: To your knowledge, had Simo Drljaca been appointed in his new -- in the position as chief of the Public Security Station by the government in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MILOS JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know anything, nor did I have the right to ask. He just came up and said, "I am the chief," and I respected him as the chief. So did all the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Jovan Simic?

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have a very brief question.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jankovic, are you sure that the day the dispatch arrived and the day the meeting was held were on the same day? Are you quite sure that this happened on the same day? Are you sure of that? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MILOS JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I am deeply convinced that the takeover was on Thursday and the dispatch arrived on Tuesday because I had just arrived from the field. And why the 29th is written here, I can't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: My question, Mr. Jankovic, is not the date but whether the dispatch arrived on the same day that the meeting was held.

utterances.speaker: MILOS JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I said that already, that the dispatch arrived an hour into the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Jovan Simic. Judge Fouad Riad? Judge Wald?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jankovic, we have no more questions for you. Thank you very much for coming, and we wish you a safe journey home. Thank you very much. The usher will see you out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see Mr. Saxon standing, but I think that Mr. Jovan Simic also wishes to tender some documents. Is it the same thing, Mr. Saxon, excuse me?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It is related, Your Honour. It is simply a clarification to reduce confusion. I simply wanted to point out to the Chamber and to all parties that the document that was tendered by Mr. Jovan Simic, D44/5, and discussed by this witness, by the last witness, has actually already been admitted. It is document 2/3.2. It was part of the documentary evidence collection submitted by the Prosecution in 1999 and admitted into evidence in March of 1999. So I simply wanted to clarify that. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Saxon. Mr. Jovan Simic?

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleague Mr. Saxon is quite right. That is one and the same document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And you'd like to have 43/5 tendered into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I feel a little lost myself now. I think that we had Exhibit 43/5 and 44/5, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two documents, that is?

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, you accept that there is a correspondence between the document already admitted into evidence and your D44 exhibit but are you not asking to tender document 43/5? You're not?

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, thank you. We take note that Defence Exhibit 44/5 corresponds to a Prosecution Exhibit numbered D2/3.2 [as interpreted], which has already been admitted into evidence. And there we have it. May we move into private session to discuss the matter of the other document? Let us move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, thank you. The meeting is adjourned until tomorrow morning, 9.20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: be reconvened on Tuesday, the 15th day of May, 2001, at 9.20 a.m.
